business: Nota (@NotaGetBot): a Telegram bot that collects receipts, invoices and handwritten delivery notes from work chats into the owner's Google Sheet and flags duplicates and arithmetic errors
by_segment: Remote investor in villas or a build, living abroad
Villa management company or villa rental operator
why_not: I would let my admin try the free 30 receipts, but 30 is gone in about a week at a café and then I am paying for something my staff may drop. She already has her Excel routine, even if it is always behind, and I am not paying monthly until I see it stick.

My bookkeeper and I already run everything through our expense app and it works well enough. I might drop one chat export in for the free 30 to see if it catches duplicates, but I'm not paying for a second tool that does half of what I already have.

The problem is real, I only look at those receipt groups when something smells wrong and I know money slips through. But I'm not handing a full export of my work chats, with transfer screenshots and bank details, to a bot I've never heard of from a company that might be gone by next season.

I'm not sending my whole work chat to a bot I've never heard of, and I'm not putting it in our group or hooking it to my Google account. Half of what I spend is parts and fuel, and the mechanics get paid cash with no receipt at all, so a report built from chat receipts wouldn't show me much I can't see in a notebook.

Half our notas are handwritten by the warung or faded thermal paper, and if the bot reads 150.000 as 15.000 I end up checking every row anyway, which is what I already do in the chat at night. I might throw the free 30 at it out of curiosity, but I would not start paying in the first month.

My boys bring handwritten nota from the toko bangunan, and I doubt a bot reads that scrawl correctly. The cheating I caught was inflated amounts the shop wrote down on request, not the same receipt sent twice, so duplicate-spotting alone doesn't catch my real problem. I'd run the free 30 and probably stop there, because I already check everything myself in Excel.

I send the bank transfers myself, so my bank statement already tells me where the money went. I might throw the free 30 documents at it out of curiosity, but I would not pay every month for a sheet I can keep myself.

Nineteen dollars is nothing to me, but I only dig into the receipts when something smells off, and for that I have Excel and could get someone to rig a bot for free. I don't feel this problem every week, so I'm not adding another subscription for it.
why_yes: I'm thousands of kilometres from the build and every night I'm scrolling the chat trying to guess what got spent, while my admin's sheet is a week behind. If it catches duplicates and wrong amounts without filtering through my own people, $35 or even $79 a month is nothing next to one padded receipt, so I'd run the free 30 on our chat export and pay if it holds up.

I already caught someone double-claiming, so I'd test it on an old chat export where I know a duplicate is hiding. If it finds that one without me pointing at it, $19 a month is nothing next to one inflated parts receipt.
flip: Seeing it read a month of our own messy handwritten notas from the villa group with almost no mistakes in the free trial, and flag a real duplicate payment I had missed.
A full first month free, so my admin can stop typing receipts for four weeks and I actually get the weekly report on my phone without anyone chasing it.
If the free 30 reads my actual handwritten nota without mistakes and flags something real I missed, like the same material bought at very different prices or a double claim, I'd pay $19 the same day.
If the free report actually caught a real overcharge or double payment on my build that I had missed, I would pay for the months the build is running and cancel afterwards.
If the free 30 documents, run on my own real handwritten nota, came back with the amounts and items right with almost nothing to correct.
If it plugged straight into Jurnal or Zoho so it fed my current setup instead of replacing it, and the free run actually found real duplicate payments or wrong amounts in my site chats.
If the free run on my own chat actually caught a duplicate payment or a wrong amount, or gave my accountant the month-end documents in a form she accepts without chasing me, I'd pay.
Another villa owner I know telling me they've used it for months and it caught real duplicate payments, so I'd know it's legit and sticking around.

A version that works without my Google account and without joining the group, where I forward only the receipts I pick, from a known local company that deletes everything after processing and says so in writing.
If the free run on my own chat turned up real money I was losing, like a part paid for twice or a fuel receipt with the wrong amount, and it covered more than the $19 a month.
If the free run on my own chat found duplicate or inflated payments worth more than a few months of the subscription, like a part paid twice or a fuel amount that doesn't match, I'd pay.
Another builder I know here using it for a few months and telling me it's fine, and a way to try it by forwarding one batch of receipts without adding it to the group or linking my Google account.
My bookkeeper telling me she already uses it with other clients and it actually cuts down what's missing at month end.
If the free report actually caught a duplicate payment or a wrong amount that cost me more than a few months of the fee, I'd pay for a month and see if it keeps finding things.

If I ran the free 30 documents on my own build chat and it caught a real duplicate or padded nota my staff sent, I'd pay on the spot.
If I run my old chat through the free 30 documents and it finds a real double payment or a wrong amount that my current app and bookkeeper missed, worth more than a few months of the fee.

If the free report actually caught duplicate payments or wrong amounts I'd missed, worth more than a month's fee, and there was a plan under 100 documents for around $9 that keeps my data in my own sheet if they shut down.
